news.summary:
Exclusive: Lewisham council’s move marks first step in Greens’ plan to create a corridor of sanctuary boroughs across London

news_drafts.headline: Lewisham forecasts £9.9m gross overspend for 2026/27, £7.0m after mitigations
news_drafts.lead:
Lewisham Council is forecasting a gross overspend of £9.9m on its 2026/27 budget, according to papers for the Housing Select Committee on 4 November. After mitigations the forecast net overspend is £7.0m. The figures come from the council's monitoring at period 4 of the financial year.

Within the gross figure, the savings report says £9.7m of savings are not being delivered. The paper attributes the in-year overspend largely to those undelivered savings.

The report says officers are working to establish which elements of the 2026/27 overspend will persist into 2027/28. A separate paper on budget reductions for 2027/28 repeats the £9.9m gross forecast and says the council continues to monitor and forecast its 2026/27 outturn. That paper does not say what offsets, if any, are planned against the gross figure.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Savings Report - M&C draft for scrutiny

news_drafts.headline: Lewisham has identified £28.497m of savings towards a £34.910m gap over 2027/28 and 2028/29
news_drafts.lead:
Lewisham Council's officers have identified £28.497m of savings towards a budget gap of £34.910m across the two financial years 2027/28 and 2028/29, according to a savings report prepared for the Healthier Communities Select Committee, which meets on 3 November 2026.

The report splits the figures by year. For 2027/28, savings of £16.888m have been identified against a gap of £20.925m. For 2028/29, the figures are £11.609m against £13.985m.

The council says the proposals put forward do not meet the budget gap. Officers will continue developing new proposals totalling at least £30m, to come forward as part of setting the 2027/28 budget. The report sets out what happens if proposals totalling £30m cannot be identified or agreed. In that case, it says, the difference "will fall to reserves to fund for 2027/28" and will immediately be added to the 2028/29 savings target, which is already £13.985m.

The report is a draft for scrutiny, so the committee will see it before the proposals are settled.

news_drafts.headline: Lewisham pension fund 119% funded at 2025 valuation, up from 97% at 2022, with a £301m surplus
news_drafts.lead:
Lewisham's pension fund was 119% funded at its latest valuation, against 97% at the previous one, according to its draft annual report for 2025-26 presented to the Pensions Committee on 15 October. The triennial valuation, the full assessment of the fund done every three years, was as at 31 March 2025. It put assets at £1.88bn and liabilities at £1.58bn, a surplus of £301m. The discount rate used to value those liabilities rose from 3.6% to 5.3% a year between the 2022 and 2025 valuations.

In the year to 31 March 2026 the fund's value rose by £155m, or 8.3%, from £1.881bn to £2.036bn. The report says this came as the membership "continues to mature" and during "a prolonged period of higher inflation", both of which increase the fund's liabilities. The fund's 12-month investment return was 9.45%, against a benchmark of 10.39%. Over five years its absolute return was 5.79%, against a benchmark of 5.65%.

Running costs fell. Administration expenses were £1.076m in 2025-26, down 22.4% from £1.387m in 2024-25. Total expenses, covering administration, oversight and investment management, fell 15.0% from £3.870m to £3.287m. Investment management fees rose 10.1%, from £1.452m to £1.598m.

findings.headline: Lewisham says its revised MTFS will follow the Autumn Budget Statement on 28 October 2026 and be published with the 2027/28 Budget Report
findings.detail: The paper says announcements in the second half of the financial year, including the Autumn Budget Statement, will inform a revised MTFS. It also refers to continuing geopolitical instability and its macroeconomic impact.
findings.matters: A revised MTFS will reset the savings target and the reliance on reserves, so the timing and content will be the next point at which the council's position can be compared with peers.
findings.quote: will inform the development of a revised MTFS, which will be published as part of the 2027/28 Budget Report

findings.headline: Lewisham's temporary accommodation households fell to 2,157 in September 2026, on a downward trajectory over three years
findings.detail: The paper attributes the trend to the transformation programme, homelessness prevention, and move-on support. It says that moving from nightly paid accommodation to acquired properties reduces costs, because nightly paid accommodation is subject to a housing benefit subsidy cap. The paper notes risk to the programme given statutory duties.
findings.matters: The subsidy cap on nightly paid accommodation means temporary accommodation volume and mix feed directly into the general fund, which is a pressure other councils with similar TA numbers also face.
findings.figures: 2,157 households in temporary accommodation (September 2026); 90% of 2011 Local Housing Allowance (subsidy cap)
findings.quote: The number of households in TA has remained on a downward trajectory over the last 3 years with 2,157 in TA in September 2026.

findings.headline: Lewisham says it is working up new proposals totalling at least £30m so that it does not need reserves to set a balanced 2027/28 budget
findings.detail: The paper says the additional proposals will come forward as part of setting the 2027/28 budget. It describes this as a way to minimise the risk of drawing on reserves to balance next year's budget.
findings.matters: The reserves position for 2027/28 depends on whether this additional £30m is found, which is the variable a finance director or lender would watch in the next budget report.
findings.figures: at least £30m (new proposals to be developed)
findings.quote: so as to minimise the risk of requiring reserves to set a balanced budget next year

findings.headline: Lewisham is forecasting a gross overspend of £9.9m for its 2026/27 outturn
findings.detail: The paper says the council continues to monitor and forecast its 2026/27 outturn, and the forecast is a gross overspend. The paper does not say what offsets, if any, are planned against it.
findings.matters: A forecast gross overspend this year reduces the headroom available for the 2027/28 budget and bears on whether reserves may be needed.
findings.quote: is forecasting a gross overspend of £9.9m

findings.headline: Lewisham has identified £16.888m of savings for 2027/28 and £11.784m for 2028/29 and 2029/30, and officers say the proposals do not meet the budget gap
findings.detail: The savings process has concluded with proposals set out in Appendices 2 to 7. The paper states that these do not meet the budget gap, so officers will develop further proposals before the 2027/28 budget is set.
findings.matters: A savings plan that the council itself says is short of its target, with the shortfall to be closed later, is the status a lender or peer finance officer would track through the budget-setting cycle.
findings.figures: £16.888m (2027/28 savings identified); £11.784m (2028/29 and 2029/30 savings identified); £20.925m and £13.985m (2027/28 and 2028/29 savings profile)
findings.quote: As the level of proposals put forward do not meet the budget gap
